entries.meta: A ranked system's place in its model's table: 1 plus the number of systems placed above it.
entries.name: Position
entries.terms: position a ranked system's place in its model's table: 1 plus the number of systems placed above it.

entries.meta: With one prompt token changed, the verifier refuses the proof (rule).
entries.name: Prompt check
entries.terms: prompt check with one prompt token changed, the verifier refuses the proof (rule).

entries.meta: On a system's page, the file the system sends with each reply for the verifier to check.
entries.name: Proof
entries.terms: proof on a system's page, the file the system sends with each reply for the verifier to check.

entries.meta: Files that let a verifier check that a reply is what a committed model produces for a prompt.
entries.name: Proof of inference
entries.terms: proof of inference files that let a verifier check that a reply is what a committed model produces for a prompt.

entries.meta: Said of a statement that a sound verifier's acceptance establishes, under the claim card's stated assumptions.
entries.name: Proved
entries.terms: proved said of a statement that a sound verifier's acceptance establishes, under the claim card's stated assumptions.

entries.meta: The program that makes a proof, and by extension whoever runs it.
entries.name: Prover
entries.terms: prover the program that makes a proof, and by extension whoever runs it.

entries.meta: The organisation that releases a proof system and its documents, or a model and its weights.
entries.name: Publisher
entries.terms: publisher the organisation that releases a proof system and its documents, or a model and its weights.

entries.meta: Sentences copied word for word from the publisher's documents at the pinned commit, each linked to its line.
entries.name: The publisher's words
entries.terms: the publisher's words sentences copied word for word from the publisher's documents at the pinned commit, each linked to its line.

entries.meta: The 8-bit copy (Q8_0) and the 4-bit copy (Q4_K_M): the original model with its weights rounded to 8 bits, and mostly to 4 bits, by llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.
entries.name: Q8_0 and Q4_K_M
entries.terms: q8_0 and q4_k_m the 8-bit copy (q8_0) and the 4-bit copy (q4_k_m): the original model with its weights rounded to 8 bits, and mostly to 4 bits, by llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.

entries.meta: Storing a model's numbers in fewer bits, which is cheaper to prove and can change replies.
entries.name: Quantization
entries.terms: quantization storing a model's numbers in fewer bits, which is cheaper to prove and can change replies.

entries.meta: An ideal hash function that gives every new input a fresh, uniformly random output.
entries.name: Random oracle
entries.terms: random oracle an ideal hash function that gives every new input a fresh, uniformly random output.

entries.meta: What a grade comes from, printed at the head of an opened petal's evidence, with "our reading" beside the grade wherever a reading of ours sets it: the publisher's words, its own sentence; our reading, with the number of points it covers, where no single sentence of the publisher's states a point, so we read it from several passages, which are linked; our test, our own runs; our rebuild, our run of the publisher's proof through its proof-checking program.
entries.name: Read as
entries.terms: read as what a grade comes from, printed at the head of an opened petal's evidence, with "our reading" beside the grade wherever a reading of ours sets it: the publisher's words, its own sentence; our reading, with the number of points it covers, where no single sentence of the publisher's states a point, so we read it from several passages, which are linked; our test, our own runs; our rebuild, our run of the publisher's proof through its proof-checking program.

entries.meta: Checking a claimed output by running the computation again and comparing.
entries.name: Recomputation
entries.terms: recomputation checking a claimed output by running the computation again and comparing.

entries.meta: Whoever acts on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, an auditor, a regulator or an inspectorate.
entries.name: Relying party
entries.terms: relying party whoever acts on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, an auditor, a regulator or an inspectorate.

entries.meta: Every proof covers all of the request's reply tokens, and with one changed (first, last or one inside) the verifier refuses it (rule).
entries.name: Reply check
entries.terms: reply check every proof covers all of the request's reply tokens, and with one changed (first, last or one inside) the verifier refuses it (rule).

entries.meta: One prompt and the reply checked for it: at Level 1, 512 prompt tokens and a 512-token greedy reply.
entries.name: Request
entries.terms: request one prompt and the reply checked for it: at level 1, 512 prompt tokens and a 512-token greedy reply.

entries.meta: What a dishonest prover can still do while its proofs are accepted.
entries.name: Residual
entries.terms: residual what a dishonest prover can still do while its proofs are accepted.

entries.meta: The publisher's prover, as published at the pin, ran three sessions from a cold start, and every reply got an accepted proof (rule).
entries.name: Run check
entries.terms: run check the publisher's prover, as published at the pin, ran three sessions from a cold start, and every reply got an accepted proof (rule).

entries.meta: Said of a guarantee that comes from checking a random part of the work, such as some replies.
entries.name: Sampled
entries.terms: sampled said of a guarantee that comes from checking a random part of the work, such as some replies.

entries.meta: A measure, in bits, of how hard it is to get a false proof accepted.
entries.name: Security level
entries.terms: security level a measure, in bits, of how hard it is to get a false proof accepted.

entries.meta: The GPU-seconds per reply that serving the request takes with no proof, on the model publisher's own release.
entries.name: Serving baseline
entries.terms: serving baseline the gpu-seconds per reply that serving the request takes with no proof, on the model publisher's own release.

entries.meta: One run of a system from a cold start on one slot's prompts: it loads the model, commits to the weights, then proves every reply (120 replies on Llama 4 Maverick, 5 on Llama 3.1 8B).
entries.name: Session
entries.terms: session one run of a system from a cold start on one slot's prompts: it loads the model, commits to the weights, then proves every reply (120 replies on llama 4 maverick, 5 on llama 3.1 8b).

entries.meta: One of three fixed sets of a model's prompts.
entries.name: Slot
entries.terms: slot one of three fixed sets of a model's prompts.

entries.meta: Two names for proof systems: SNARKs (succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge) and STARKs.
entries.name: SNARK and STARK
entries.terms: snark and stark two names for proof systems: snarks (succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge) and starks.

entries.meta: The property that a verifier refuses proofs of false statements, except with a probability the security level bounds.
entries.name: Soundness
entries.terms: soundness the property that a verifier refuses proofs of false statements, except with a probability the security level bounds.

entries.meta: The probability, as the publisher states it, that a verifier accepts a proof of a false statement: the bound behind soundness.
entries.name: Soundness error
entries.terms: soundness error the probability, as the publisher states it, that a verifier accepts a proof of a false statement: the bound behind soundness.

entries.meta: The proposition that an accepted proof establishes.
entries.name: Statement
entries.terms: statement the proposition that an accepted proof establishes.

entries.meta: The part of a session after its first group of proofs, when proofs come out at an even pace.
entries.name: Steady state
entries.terms: steady state the part of a session after its first group of proofs, when proofs come out at an even pace.

entries.meta: Our statistical test finds an average above a threshold at the usual 5% level: p < 0.05 in a paired sign-flip test over the prompts.
entries.name: Shown above
entries.terms: shown above our statistical test finds an average above a threshold at the usual 5% level: p < 0.05 in a paired sign-flip test over the prompts.

entries.meta: A protocol that convinces a verifier of a polynomial's sum over exponentially many points with one random evaluation.
entries.name: Sumcheck
entries.terms: sumcheck a protocol that convinces a verifier of a polynomial's sum over exponentially many points with one random evaluation.

entries.meta: A mathematical result with its proof.
entries.name: Theorem
entries.terms: theorem a mathematical result with its proof.

entries.meta: The unit of text a model reads and writes, a word or part of one, stored as an integer.
entries.name: Token
entries.terms: token the unit of text a model reads and writes, a word or part of one, stored as an integer.

entries.meta: The request's reply tokens over the GPU-seconds one reply took, on one GPU, printed in tokens/s per GPU with the GPU named.
entries.name: Tokens per second
entries.terms: tokens per second the request's reply tokens over the gpu-seconds one reply took, on one gpu, printed in tokens/s per gpu with the gpu named.

entries.meta: Whether checking a proof relies on anyone's honesty besides the mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware maker's key (petal).
entries.name: Trust assumptions
entries.terms: trust assumptions whether checking a proof relies on anyone's honesty besides the mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware maker's key (petal).

entries.meta: A hardware enclave (TEE) in a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's owner.
entries.name: Trusted execution environment
entries.terms: trusted execution environment a hardware enclave (tee) in a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's owner.

entries.meta: A one-time step that makes public parameters from a secret whose holder could forge proofs, as in KZG commitments.
entries.name: Trusted setup
entries.terms: trusted setup a one-time step that makes public parameters from a secret whose holder could forge proofs, as in kzg commitments.

entries.meta: Checking a claim against evidence that holds even if the claimant has a reason to cheat.
entries.name: Verification
entries.terms: verification checking a claim against evidence that holds even if the claimant has a reason to cheat.

entries.meta: The program that checks a proof against the commitment and the prompt, and accepts or refuses.
entries.name: Verifier
entries.terms: verifier the program that checks a proof against the commitment and the prompt, and accepts or refuses.

entries.meta: The verifier reached every verdict with no copy of the model and no GPU (rule).
entries.name: Verify without weights check
entries.terms: verify without weights check the verifier reached every verdict with no copy of the model and no gpu (rule).

entries.meta: The learned numbers a model is made of, about 8 billion in Llama 3.1 8B.
entries.name: Weights
entries.terms: weights the learned numbers a model is made of, about 8 billion in llama 3.1 8b.

entries.meta: A figure that counts a session's GPU time from the start of its commit call to its last proof (the commit, generation and proving; loading the model before the commit is not counted), divided by its replies.
entries.name: Whole session
entries.terms: whole session a figure that counts a session's gpu time from the start of its commit call to its last proof (the commit, generation and proving; loading the model before the commit is not counted), divided by its replies.

entries.meta: Everything the prover uses to build a proof and the verifier does not see.
entries.name: Witness
entries.terms: witness everything the prover uses to build a proof and the verifier does not see.

entries.meta: The property that a proof shows nothing beyond the truth of its statement: all a verifier sees could be simulated without the weights.
entries.name: Zero knowledge
entries.terms: zero knowledge the property that a proof shows nothing beyond the truth of its statement: all a verifier sees could be simulated without the weights.
